title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: CURTIS'S PADDLE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Curtis Boone, thirty-four, a pool repairman in Mesa, Arizona.
In high school, he was the star point guard. He still talks like it.
Then he met a seventy-four-year-old woman with a pickleball paddle.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: ELEVEN TO ZERO
segments.quote: Winning is great, sure, but if you are really going to do something in life, the secret is learning how to lose.
segments.author: Wilma Rudolph
lines: At the park, Curtis laughed at the pickleball courts. Ping-pong for grandmas, he said.
Marjorie Flanagan, a retired crop-duster pilot, handed him a paddle. One game, hotshot.
She beat him eleven to zero. That night he found a line from the sprinter Wilma Rudolph:
Winning is great, sure, but if you are really going to do something in life, the secret is learning how to lose.
Next morning, Curtis knocked on Marjorie's door and asked for lessons.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: TOO MANY RULES
segments.quote: You can't think and hit at the same time.
segments.author: Yogi Berra
lines: Marjorie taught him the kitchen, the dink, the two-bounce rule. Curtis froze on every ball.
Marjorie grinned and quoted the baseball great Yogi Berra:
You can't think and hit at the same time.
So Curtis stopped thinking, watched the ball, and hit it. Into the net. But still.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE GARAGE DOOR
segments.quote: Practice yourself, for heaven's sake, in little things; and thence proceed to greater.
segments.author: Epictetus
lines: Curtis wanted to smash every ball like a slam dunk.
Marjorie taped a note to his water bottle, from the Greek teacher Epictetus:
Practice yourself, for heaven's sake, in little things; and thence proceed to greater.
So every dawn, before the heat, Curtis tapped soft shots against his garage door. His neighbors bought earplugs.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE PARTNER
segments.quote: We are made for co-operation, like feet, like hands, like eyelids, like the rows of the upper and lower teeth.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: In March, they entered the city tournament as partners. Curtis chased every ball, even hers.
Marjorie read him a line from the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius:
We are made for co-operation, like feet, like hands, like eyelids, like the rows of the upper and lower teeth.
Curtis laughed. Fine, he'd be the bottom teeth. He stayed on his side, and they won four straight.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LINE CALL
segments.quote: I would prefer even to fail with honor than win by cheating.
segments.author: Sophocles
lines: In the semifinal, at match point, the other team's shot hit the line. Nobody else saw it.
Curtis could call it out. Then he remembered a line from Sophocles on Marjorie's fridge:
I would prefer even to fail with honor than win by cheating.
He called it in. The crowd clapped. And they still won the next point.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FINAL
segments.quote: The softest things in the world overcome the hardest things in the world.
segments.author: Lao Tzu
lines: The final was against two young guys who hit like cannons. Curtis and Marjorie fell behind, two to nine.
At the timeout, Marjorie quoted the old Chinese teacher Lao Tzu:
The softest things in the world overcome the hardest things in the world.
So they went soft. Dink, dink, dink. The young guys hit the fence. Curtis and Marjorie won, eleven to nine.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Learn to lose. Stop overthinking. Start small. Share the court. Play fair. Go soft.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Learn to lose. Stop overthinking. Start small. Share the court. Play fair. Go soft.
Me, I tried pickleball once. I'm still looking for the ball.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
